topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture themes and outlines the intended learning outcomes for studying cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Clonal selection and epigenetic drivers in tumor initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how both genetic clonal selection and non-mutational epigenetic alterations drive the early stages of tumor development.

topics.label: Cell of origin and the cancer stem cell model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stem cell hierarchies and specific cells of origin determine tumor initiation and propagation across different tissues.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory promotion of tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how environmental and local inflammatory stimuli provide the necessary permissive signals and stromal support for tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Technologies for analyzing tumor evolution and spatial architecture
topics.groupedBecause: It details the single-cell and spatial profiling methodologies used to map tumor heterogeneity and cell-microenvironment interactions.

topics.label: Multifactorial synthesis of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It synthesizes the interplay among mutational burden, cell of origin, microenvironmental inflammation, and Darwinian selection into a unified model of cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the concluding remarks for the session and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
